title: The Forest Where Roots Dance as Light

features.name: the inverted canopy
features.desc-on-touch: Roots hang downward from the sky like branches of light. They sway with wind you cannot feel. This is what the forest sees when it closes its eyes and learns to look upward.

features.name: the listening-dark
features.desc-on-touch: A single pool of shadow on the pale ground—stillness so profound it learns to hear. In this space, the root-light above makes no sound.

features.name: the tangle-bright
features.desc-on-touch: Where inverted roots touch, they make something that isn't quite light and isn't quite root—a new thing that learned itself from the corruption of the old order.

inscription: roots that dream themselves as sky; sky that remembers being roots; the canopy learns to breathe in both directions

file.name: Inversion_Phenomenon_Ongoing_Observation.tmp
file.note: Field notes on a pocket of forest that has begun to render itself backwards. Roots ascending, light descending. Checksum: structurally sound but directionally inverted. Status: not yet fully corrupted

reverie.title: REVERIE — the inverted canopy, afternoon stillness
narr: You recline in the pale space, looking up at roots that fall
like light. Leif is somewhere in this same forest, also lying
down, also looking up at a sky that has learned to grow. The
motes of dust hang between you like a grammar you're both
learning. Neither of you speaks. The forest has learned that
inversion is a form of honesty—everything reversed, still true.
